hero_current_student_label: High school senior majoring in science
story_para1: I was born and raised in Cupramontana and since childhood I've always felt the need to express myself, invent and build things. My dream was clear: to become a successful YouTuber. That idea made my eyes sparkle because it let me combine my passions: speaking in front of a camera, telling my own stories and shaping each video from scratch.
story_para2: On August 10, 2015, at nine years old, I uploaded my first video. It was the start of a three-year adventure during which I posted 213 videos, all still online. I recorded gameplays, explained historical curiosities with my brother, made magic tutorials, experiments and video edits. I did everything with the tools I had and what I could teach myself. I began using early editing software, took care of the graphics and tried to improve step by step. It wasn't just a pastime: I was learning to create content and manage a personal project with a weekly schedule.
story_para3: In middle school many suggested I choose a scientific high school, but I'd already decided on IT. I felt my future was there and wanted to learn programming. To me code wasn't just technique, but a way to develop something combining logic, usefulness and imagination.
story_para4: Outside school, driven by curiosity, I got closer and closer to design. I alternated Fusion 360 with exercises on Figma, but above all I spent hours on Photoshop, experimenting, trying and starting over. I enjoyed creating but also figuring out how to make something look professional — whether an interface, a logo or a poster.
story_para5: It was a different way to express myself yet complementary to coding: code gave me structure, design freedom. And I needed both.
story_para6: When I started high school my approach to life changed: after years on social media I felt the need to step back and focus on myself. It wasn't rejection, but an evolution. I began working out, studying more consciously, developing personal projects I didn't feel like sharing but that truly helped me grow and improve.
story_para7: Today I keep moving between code and design, between technology and creativity. Most of all I keep doing what comes naturally: learning, exploring, creating. In my own way.
marconi_para1: The first two years at Marconi Pieralisi were partly affected by the pandemic: many classes were remote and subjects not very specific. Only from the third year did the program become more engaging thanks to courses like Computer Science, Systems and Networks, TPSIT and Artificial Intelligence. AI in particular fascinated me with its logic-based approach and constantly evolving models.
marconi_para2: Alongside technical studies I also focused on human aspects: the civic education course — mixing law, current events and environment — helped me develop critical thinking and look at things from different perspectives.
marconi_para3: In the fourth year I ran for student representative. I was elected and threw myself into the role. It was challenging and taught me what it means to speak up and represent others even at delicate times.
marconi_para4: Among the most formative experiences were the two editions of the Hackathon Innova Young in Ancona. In 2023 I was the youngest and handled all the visual side of the project. In 2024 I was team leader: I managed the group, made quick decisions and learned how to truly lead. We placed third both times.
marconi_para5: If I could go back, I'd choose this school a hundred times again. I was also lucky to immediately get along with my class, a group full of diverse personalities to share every experience with. The teachers made the difference too: available, passionate, able to pass on enthusiasm and make even distant topics interesting. It's not common to find teachers who believe in what they teach and push you to give your best; thanks to them these years were so rich, meaningful and wonderful.
music_para1: Music isn't just a hobby: it's an integral part of my everyday life, always with me, helping me focus, clear my mind and give rhythm even to the busiest days. I listen to huge amounts whenever I have headphones handy. I don't stick to a single genre: I naturally move from experimental electronic to rap, from international pop to more alternative, hybrid sounds. I love surprising myself, discovering new sonic languages, but also returning to those albums that become 'home' in certain periods.
music_para2: I love the energy of concerts: whenever I can, I attend live performances because on stage music becomes a shared, tangible experience. Seeing it come to life reminds me every time why I started playing.
music_para3: I began studying music at four, joining the course of the Don N. Bonanni band in Cupramontana; at six I picked up the drums. They've always been my instrument, the one that lets me express myself freely. Over time I've kept playing in different contexts: workshops, gigs, small groups and, above all, within the same band I still collaborate with.
music_para4: In recent years this passion has become something to share. Today I support the music course teachers as an educator, entertainer and percussion instructor, both during the summer camp and in annual classes. I work with children and teens, trying to convey not only the basics but above all enthusiasm and respect for what music can offer: listening, coordination, teamwork, creativity.
music_para5: Taking on the role of mentor showed me a new side of this passion. One of the most exciting experiences was seeing my students perform at the final recital. I was very anxious, feeling the responsibility of the moment, but they were amazing! They played with focus, courage and joy, and it was wonderful to see them succeed in what we had prepared together. I'm deeply proud: that evening further strengthened my bond with music and teaching.
future_para1: For many years I pictured my future in Milan, convinced I would study and build my career there. The idea of enrolling in Industrial Design came at fourteen and over time became a concrete goal. This year I took the admission test both for Industrial Design at Politecnico di Milano and for Interaction Design in Lecco, believing both could be a consistent step forward.
future_para2: The Industrial Design ranking came out first and, since I was within the available spots, it offered me the chance to enrol immediately. Yet inside I felt a change of direction: my interests were shifting toward design focused on experience, on the relationship between people and technology, on building effective interactions. I gave up that opportunity — a bit risky but with equal conviction — hoping to make it into Interaction Design. Luckily it worked out as I wished.
future_para3: The program in Lecco is entirely in English and still young — next year will only be the second. That's precisely why it attracts me even more: it's a dynamic path, looking to the future, combining technology, creativity, design and care for people, all things I relate to.
future_para4: During my campus visit I immediately found a welcoming environment: modern, well-kept and above all calm. Lecco gave me a sense of balance, far from Milan's frenzy, and I think this will help me live university more serenely, deeply and productively. The course will start in September but I'm already excited: I hope it's the right context to grow, learn and challenge myself in what I'm most passionate about.
future_para5: Looking further ahead, I imagine founding something of my own. I still don't know what shape it will take — a studio, an independent project or something else I can't yet define — but I'd love to be the one to start it, build it from scratch and sustain it over time, almost like raising a child. What matters to me is to have something I don't just want profit from, but that I want to care for with dedication, creativity and a deep sense of responsibility.
